0.en: Aiden got to the station a quarter of an hour later, out of breath. He had a glass jar in one hand and a pair of long kitchen tongs in the other.
0.id: Aiden sampai di stasiun seperempat jam kemudian, terengah-engah. Ia membawa stoples kaca di satu tangan dan sepasang capit dapur panjang di tangan yang lain.

1.en: Paul was still kneeling by the trough. He looked at the tongs.
1.id: Paul masih berlutut di samping talang. Ia memandang capit itu.

3.en: They were in the station kitchen.

5.en: Mark lifted the first lid section himself, slowly, the way he had closed it. It came up clean on the rubber strips and didn't drag any water with it. There was hardly any water left to drag. A thin film lay across the bottom of the trough, and at the far end, pressed flat against the metal where the last of it had drained away, lay the gnat.
5.id: Mark sendiri yang mengangkat bagian tutup yang pertama, pelan-pelan, seperti waktu ia menutupnya. Tutup itu terangkat bersih dari strip karet dan tidak menyeret air sedikit pun. Memang hampir tidak ada air tersisa untuk terseret. Lapisan tipis tergenang di dasar talang, dan di ujung yang jauh, tertekan rata ke logam di tempat sisa air terakhir terkuras, tergeletak agas itu.

6.en: It didn't move. Its wings were stuck down along its back, and its legs were folded under it.
6.id: Agas itu tidak bergerak. Sayapnya menempel di sepanjang punggungnya, dan kakinya terlipat di bawah tubuhnya.

7.en: Aiden reached in with the tongs and lifted it out, carefully, the way Jack had once seen a jeweler lift a stone. It was the size of a cat and it weighed almost nothing. He laid it in the jar and screwed the lid on and held it up to the window.
7.id: Aiden menjulurkan capit ke dalam dan mengangkatnya keluar, hati-hati, seperti cara Jack dulu pernah melihat seorang tukang perhiasan mengangkat batu permata. Agas itu seukuran kucing dan nyaris tak berbobot. Aiden meletakkannya di dalam stoples, memutar tutupnya rapat, lalu mengangkatnya ke jendela.

8.en: Lena watched him over her clipboard.
8.id: Lena memperhatikannya dari balik papan klipnya.

9.en: What do you want it for?

11.en: I want to know what it is. And what it was eating, before it got stuck in a drop. If the spider eats gnats, and gnats eat something, I'd like to know what the something is. Everything out there is eating something. We just don't know the list yet.
11.id: Aku mau tahu ini apa. Dan apa yang dimakannya, sebelum terjebak di dalam tetesan. Kalau laba-laba itu makan agas, dan agas makan sesuatu, aku ingin tahu sesuatu itu apa. Semua yang ada di luar sana memakan sesuatu. Kita saja yang belum tahu daftarnya.

12.en: Mark had his whiteboard out again. He had wiped it down to the four words in the corner, Cold, Clear, Gray, Covered, and under them he had drawn a line down the middle.
12.id: Mark sudah mengeluarkan papan tulisnya lagi. Ia sudah menghapusnya sampai tinggal empat kata di pojok, Dingin, Cerah, Kelabu, Tertutup, dan di bawahnya ia menarik garis tepat di tengah.

15.en: The board. It came straight at us, and the board took it.
15.id: Papannya. Tetesan itu meluncur lurus ke arah kita, dan papan itu yang menahannya.

17.en: The collar. My glove came back dry.
17.id: Kerahnya. Sarung tanganku pulang dalam keadaan kering.

21.en: Unit Four spoke from the doorway, a little hesitantly.
21.id: Unit Empat bicara dari ambang pintu, agak ragu-ragu.

22.en: Walking it back on the rope. Nobody had to carry it.
22.id: Menuntunnya mundur dengan tali. Tidak ada yang harus mengangkatnya.

23.en: Mark wrote Rope, and then he looked at Unit Four for a moment longer than he needed to.
23.id: Mark menulis Tali, lalu memandang Unit Empat sedikit lebih lama daripada yang perlu.

24.en: That was a good thing to do twice. Tying off the hitch.
24.id: Itu bagus, melakukannya dua kali. Mengikat tali di kait derek.

25.en: Unit Four went red and didn't say anything.
25.id: Wajah Unit Empat memerah dan ia tidak berkata apa-apa.

26.en: Mark moved the marker across the line.
26.id: Mark memindahkan spidolnya ke seberang garis.

29.en: We set it in the wrong place. In the dark, we put it under the biggest drop, and the biggest drop is under the front door. We spent two minutes of gray moving it. Two minutes we didn't have.
29.id: Kita menaruhnya di tempat yang salah. Dalam gelap, kita menaruhnya di bawah tetesan paling besar, dan tetesan paling besar ada di bawah pintu depan. Kita menghabiskan dua menit kelabu untuk memindahkannya. Dua menit yang tidak kita punya.

30.en: Mark wrote Moved it. Lost time.

32.en: And it leaked. Not much. Out of the corners, when you walked it back. There's a wet line from the end of the road to the cart. I saw it on the feed while you were coming in.
32.id: Dan talangnya bocor. Tidak banyak. Dari sudut-sudutnya, waktu kalian menuntunnya mundur. Ada garis basah dari ujung jalan sampai ke kereta. Aku melihatnya di tayangan waktu kalian dalam perjalanan kembali.

33.en: Paul sat back on his heels.

34.en: I'll seal the corners. And I'll build you a second one. Narrower. So two people can lift it full, if it comes to that.
34.id: Saya akan menyegel sudut-sudutnya. Dan saya akan membuatkan yang kedua. Lebih sempit. Supaya dua orang bisa mengangkatnya dalam keadaan penuh, kalau sampai perlu.

35.en: Mark wrote Corners. Then he stood and looked at the board with his arms folded, and nobody said anything for a while.
35.id: Mark menulis Sudut. Lalu ia berdiri memandangi papan tulis itu dengan tangan terlipat, dan untuk beberapa saat tak ada yang berkata apa-apa.

36.en: Lena broke the silence. She didn't sound unhappy. She sounded like a woman doing a sum she had already done.
36.id: Lena memecah keheningan. Ia tidak terdengar sedih. Ia terdengar seperti perempuan yang sedang mengerjakan hitungan yang sudah pernah ia kerjakan.

37.en: A hundred and ten liters. I'm sending it to the kitchens. They've got pots big enough to boil it, and every liter they cook with today is a liter they don't take from the tanks.
37.id: Seratus sepuluh liter. Aku kirim ke dapur-dapur. Mereka punya panci yang cukup besar untuk merebusnya, dan setiap liter yang mereka pakai memasak hari ini adalah satu liter yang tidak mereka ambil dari tangki.

38.en: She looked at the gauge on the wall, and tapped the glass.
38.id: Ia memandang alat ukur di dinding, lalu mengetuk kacanya.

39.en: Which brings me to the tanks. I read them at six. Twenty-five thousand. If we'd used thirteen-fifty a day since the sixth, it would say twenty-five six.
39.id: Dan itu membawaku ke soal tangki. Aku membacanya jam enam. Dua puluh lima ribu. Kalau kita memakai seribu tiga ratus lima puluh sehari sejak tanggal enam, angkanya mestinya dua puluh lima ribu enam ratus.

40.en: Jack did the math before he wanted to.
40.id: Jack sudah menghitungnya sebelum ia mau.

42.en: Fifteen hundred, give or take. People are being careful, and it still isn't thirteen-fifty. Somebody's mother needs a bath. Somebody's tomatoes are dying. At fifteen hundred, we have about sixteen days.
42.id: Seribu lima ratus, kurang lebih. Orang-orang sudah berhati-hati, dan tetap saja bukan seribu tiga ratus lima puluh. Ibu seseorang perlu mandi. Tomat seseorang sekarat. Dengan seribu lima ratus, kita punya kira-kira enam belas hari.

43.en: Sixteen days. Jack looked at the four words in the corner of the board, and then at the hundred and ten liters on Lena's clipboard. It was the best morning they'd had since the town shrank. It would keep the whole town in water for not quite two hours.
43.id: Enam belas hari. Jack memandang empat kata di pojok papan tulis, lalu seratus sepuluh liter di papan klip Lena. Itu pagi terbaik yang mereka alami sejak kota ini menyusut. Air itu akan mencukupi seluruh kota selama hampir dua jam.

44.en: Mark had seen him do the math.

46.en: One shake is a hundred and ten liters. On a clear, cold morning. And there aren't clear, cold mornings every day.
46.id: Satu goyangan itu seratus sepuluh liter. Di pagi yang cerah dan dingin. Dan pagi yang cerah dan dingin tidak datang setiap hari.

47.en: Aiden turned the jar slowly in his hands.
47.id: Aiden memutar stoples itu pelan-pelan di tangannya.

48.en: And every shake brings one of these down. Kicking. Within sight of its front door.
48.id: Dan setiap goyangan menjatuhkan satu dari ini. Menendang-nendang. Masih kelihatan dari pintu depannya.

49.en: Mark wrote that at the bottom of the board, and underlined it.
49.id: Mark menuliskan itu di bagian bawah papan tulis, lalu menggarisbawahinya.

51.en: Here's what I'll agree to. Not again today. One leaf near that retreat on any morning. Never the one under it. If you want more water than that, find me somewhere else to shake.
51.id: Ini yang bisa kusetujui. Tidak lagi hari ini. Satu daun di dekat tempat persembunyian itu, pagi mana pun. Jangan pernah yang ada di bawahnya. Kalau kalian mau air lebih dari itu, carikan aku tempat lain untuk menggoyang.

52.en: Lena's console chimed, and Sarah's voice came out of the speaker. She sounded wide awake.
52.id: Konsol Lena berdenting, dan suara Sarah keluar dari pengeras suara. Ia terdengar segar dan terjaga penuh.

53.en: There's somewhere else. There's the end of every road.
53.id: Ada tempat lain. Ada ujung setiap jalan.

54.id: Mark mengernyit ke arah pengeras suara.

55.en: Nobody's going to the end of every road.
55.id: Tidak ada yang akan pergi ke ujung setiap jalan.

56.en: Sarah's voice sharpened a little, the way it did when she was right and knew it.
56.id: Suara Sarah sedikit menajam, seperti biasanya kalau ia benar dan tahu itu.

57.en: Nobody has to. There are cameras on all of them. Lena, when did anybody last look at the other feeds?
57.id: Tidak perlu ada yang pergi. Ada kamera di semuanya. Lena, kapan terakhir kali ada yang melihat tayangan-tayangan lain?

58.en: Lena was already scrolling. She stopped, and scrolled back, and her face changed.
58.id: Lena sudah menggulir layar. Ia berhenti, menggulir kembali, dan raut wajahnya berubah.

59.en: The sixth. Most of them. We put everyone on the western road after the spider.
59.id: Tanggal enam. Sebagian besar. Kita mengerahkan semua orang ke jalan barat setelah ada laba-laba itu.

60.en: Then I'll look. From the couch. I'll find every leaf tip that hangs over asphalt, and every drop on it, and every bag of silk above it. Mark gets a list. He likes lists.
60.id: Kalau begitu aku yang lihat. Dari sofa. Akan kucari setiap ujung daun yang menggantung di atas aspal, dan setiap tetesan di ujung itu, dan setiap kantong sutra di atasnya. Mark dapat daftar. Dia suka daftar.

61.en: Mark looked at the speaker for a long moment.
61.id: Mark memandangi pengeras suara itu cukup lama.

62.en: Doctor Mercer's going to say that's work.
62.id: Dokter Mercer bakal bilang itu kerja.

63.en: Doctor Mercer said watching is fine. This is watching. It's just more of it.
63.id: Dokter Mercer bilang mengawasi boleh. Ini mengawasi. Cuma lebih banyak saja.

64.en: Jack heard Doctor Mercer's own words in that, exactly. So did Mark. He uncapped the marker again and wrote, at the top of a fresh column: Other roads. Sarah.
64.id: Jack mendengar kata-kata Dokter Mercer sendiri di situ, persis. Mark juga. Ia membuka tutup spidol lagi dan menulis, di puncak kolom baru: Jalan-jalan lain. Sarah.

65.en: Doctor Mercer came to the house at eight. She took Sarah's pressure, and then took it again, and wrote it down without a word. Then she looked at the notebook on Sarah's knee, which now had a map drawn in the back of it, every road in town with a small circle where it ended.
65.id: Dokter Mercer datang ke rumah pukul delapan. Ia mengukur tekanan darah Sarah, lalu mengukurnya lagi, dan mencatatnya tanpa sepatah kata. Lalu ia memandang buku catatan di lutut Sarah, yang sekarang berisi peta yang digambar di halaman belakangnya, setiap jalan di kota dengan lingkaran kecil di tempat jalan itu berakhir.

70.en: Doctor Mercer looked at her for a long moment, then at the number.
70.id: Dokter Mercer memandangnya cukup lama, lalu memandang angkanya.

71.en: Same as last night. The little better is holding. I'll take that. Keep holding it.
71.id: Sama dengan semalam. Yang sedikit lebih baik itu bertahan. Saya terima. Pertahankan.

72.en: She turned to Jack, peeled back the corner of the dressing on his hand, and frowned. Then she peeled it back a little more.
72.id: Ia berbalik ke Jack, mengelupas sudut perban di tangannya, lalu mengernyit. Lalu ia mengelupasnya sedikit lagi.

75.en: Somebody finally kept a bag dry.
75.id: Akhirnya ada yang berhasil menjaga kantongnya tetap kering.

76.en: She pressed the tape back down.

77.en: Pink. No worse. Whose idea was the collar?
77.id: Merah muda. Tidak memburuk. Siapa yang punya ide kerah itu?

79.en: Tell Paul I said thank you. Don't tell him I said it twice.
79.id: Sampaikan ke Paul, saya bilang terima kasih. Jangan bilang saya mengatakannya dua kali.

80.en: On her way out, she stopped by the crib. It had both its rails on now. It stood straight.
80.id: Dalam perjalanan keluar, ia berhenti di dekat boks bayi. Kedua pagarnya sudah terpasang sekarang. Boks itu berdiri tegak.

81.en: She looked at it, and almost smiled.

83.en: Jack sat on the floor with the instructions for a while after she'd gone, trying to work out what step eleven wanted from him and failing. Sarah lay on the couch with the tablet. She had started with the western road and meant to work her way around the whole town, one feed at a time.
83.id: Setelah Dokter Mercer pergi, Jack duduk di lantai dengan buku petunjuk selama beberapa waktu, mencoba memahami apa yang diminta langkah kesebelas darinya, dan gagal. Sarah berbaring di sofa dengan tabletnya. Ia sudah mulai dari jalan barat dan berniat menyisir seluruh kota, satu tayangan demi satu tayangan.

84.en: She went quiet. Not the quiet of someone reading. The other kind.
84.id: Ia terdiam. Bukan diamnya orang yang sedang membaca. Diam yang lain.

85.en: Jack. Come and look at this.

86.en: He sat on the edge of the couch. She had the western road up. Not the live feed. The recording from that morning, a little after seven. The timestamp in the corner read seven oh four.
86.id: Jack duduk di tepi sofa. Sarah sedang membuka jalan barat. Bukan tayangan langsung. Rekaman dari pagi itu, sedikit lewat pukul tujuh. Stempel waktu di pojok menunjukkan tujuh lewat empat.

87.en: The sun was full on the road end. The trough was gone. The puddles from the shower lay on the asphalt in front of the place where it had stood, flat and shining. From them, a thin, wet line ran back across the road toward the cart. The line the corners had left.
87.id: Matahari sudah penuh menyinari ujung jalan. Talang itu sudah tidak ada. Genangan-genangan dari hujan butir air tadi terhampar di aspal di depan tempat talang itu berdiri, pipih dan berkilau. Dari genangan itu, sebuah garis basah yang tipis membentang kembali melintasi jalan ke arah kereta. Garis yang ditinggalkan sudut-sudut talang.

88.en: The spider was on the asphalt.

89.en: It had come down the stem, and onto the soil, and onto the road, in the short, low bursts he knew now. It stood over the nearest puddle with its face lowered into it. It was drinking.
89.id: Ia sudah turun dari batang, ke tanah, lalu ke jalan, dalam sentakan-sentakan pendek dan rendah yang kini dikenal Jack. Ia berdiri di atas genangan terdekat dengan wajah tertunduk ke dalamnya. Ia sedang minum.

90.en: Then it lifted its face, and moved to the next one. And the next. And then it was on the wet line, following it across the asphalt, three steps, stop, three steps, stop, toward the cart.
90.id: Lalu ia mengangkat wajahnya, dan pindah ke genangan berikutnya. Dan berikutnya lagi. Lalu ia sudah berada di garis basah itu, mengikutinya melintasi aspal, tiga langkah, berhenti, tiga langkah, berhenti, ke arah kereta.

91.en: About halfway, the line ended, where the sun had already dried the road. The spider stopped there. It stood on the last of the wet for a long time. Its front end turned slowly, left and right.
91.id: Kira-kira di tengah jalan, garis itu berakhir, di tempat matahari sudah mengeringkan jalan. Laba-laba itu berhenti di sana. Ia berdiri di sisa basah terakhir untuk waktu yang lama. Bagian depan tubuhnya berputar pelan, ke kiri dan ke kanan.

92.en: Then it turned around and went back.

94.en: Nobody saw this. Not live. I'd switched to the station camera to watch you unload. Aiden stopped when you closed the lid.
94.id: Tidak ada yang melihat ini. Tidak secara langsung. Aku sudah pindah ke kamera stasiun untuk melihat kalian membongkar muatan. Aiden berhenti waktu kalian menutup tutupnya.

95.en: Jack didn't say anything. Neither did she.
95.id: Jack tidak berkata apa-apa. Sarah juga tidak.

96.en: On the screen, the spider climbed the stem with nothing in its jaws and went into the silk. The road end was empty again, wet and shining in the sun.
96.id: Di layar, laba-laba itu memanjat batang tanpa apa pun di rahangnya dan masuk ke dalam sutra. Ujung jalan itu kosong lagi, basah dan berkilau di bawah matahari.
